system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. The cap, thresholds and claims period are below our positions. Title and fundamental claims are folded into the general regime. Fraud has no carve-out. Disclosure and buyer-knowledge protections are gutted. Three completion-critical items (Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses) are left unresolved. None of the Seller's positions should be accepted as drafted.

## Preliminary point: the "FINAL / settled at principal level" claim

The Seller's preamble says these positions "were settled at principal level by both deal teams" and are "not intended to be re-opened." We should not treat that as true.

- Our playbook records that **Amelia Frost has given no written authority** for any fallback (the 20% cap or the 18-month period). Nothing in the Seller's papers identifies an approval, a date or a document.
- The "market context" (caps of 10–20%, baskets of about 1%, 12–18 month periods, buyer-knowledge qualifiers) is the Seller's advocacy, not an agreed benchmark. It does not change our positions.
- **Action:** Before the mark-up goes out, confirm internally with Amelia Frost that no principal-level agreement exists. Then reply that the draft is not agreed and remains open.

## Material departures and recommended pushback

### 1. General cap (cl 12.1): Seller wants 20% / AUD 4.8m; we want 25% / AUD 6.0m
- The Seller's figure is exactly our *conditional fallback*. Accepting it now would concede the fallback without the required authority and give away AUD 1.2m of cover for nothing.
- **Push back:** Restate 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is available. That fallback may only be used with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft.

### 2. Thresholds (cl 12.2): Seller wants AUD 25k de minimis and AUD 250k basket, excess only
- Both thresholds are five times our position (AUD 5k / AUD 50k).
- The **"excess only" (deductible) mechanism** is a separate and significant concession. With a AUD 250k deductible, the first quarter-million of every valid claim is permanently lost to us.
- A AUD 25k de minimis would also screen out many individually modest but real SaaS claims, such as contract, data or payroll items.
- **Push back:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000 as a **tipping basket**, so the Seller is liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.

### 3. Claims period (cl 12.3/13): Seller wants 18 months; we want 24 months
- 18 months is our fallback and needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **Push back:** 24 months after Completion.

### 4. "Limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13)
- This is a **hidden general-regime override**. It would pull title, capacity, tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants into the general cap, threshold and time-limit regime by default.
- The playbook requires these categories to be kept separate.
- **Push back:** Reverse the default. General limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. Each other category gets its own expressly stated regime.

### 5. Fundamental / Title warranties: Seller wants them under the general caps and time limits
- "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap our recovery for failure of title at 20%. This is the core of what we are buying.
- **Push back:** A separate regime for Fundamental/Title claims:
  - 100% cap (AUD 24m);
  - a claims period of at least six years;
  - outside the basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.

### 6. Fraud carve-out: absent from the Seller's draft; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature"
- As drafted, this purports to limit the Seller's liability even for fraud and wilful concealment. Under NSW law, clauses of this kind may not ultimately protect a fraudulent party. We should not leave enforceability to be fought out later.
- The playbook position is non-negotiable and **no one, including the deal team, may waive it.**
- **Push back:** Insert an express carve-out from all caps, baskets, de minimis, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions. It should cover fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct by the Seller, its officers, agents and advisers, to the maximum extent enforceable.

### 7. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2)
- The letter deems disclosed "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the whole data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and publicly searchable records. This is exactly the whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure our playbook rejects.
- Para 1.4 (no admission of breach, materiality, or that any consent is required) further dilutes the specific disclosures.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete paras 1.1 and 1.2.
  - Disclosures count only if they are **specific and fair**, meaning they identify the warranty and give enough detail for us to assess nature and scope.
  - Narrow para 1.4 so it cannot undermine a specific disclosure or a specific indemnity.
- **Timing point:** The letter speaks as at **22 September 2026**, which is now about six weeks stale. Require an updated letter, with disclosure against warranties repeated at Completion limited to specific new matters, and with our right to treat material new disclosures as giving rise to claims or termination rights.

### 8. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- The clause excludes any matter known to the Buyer *or its advisers*, *including anything discoverable from the data room or public records*. This is a blanket exclusion and would, in effect, reverse the warranty package.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete the clause.
  - If any qualifier survives, it must refer to the **actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals**. Seller-side knowledge qualifiers in the warranties must use **named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry**.
  - Buyer knowledge must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### 9. Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)
- Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. This is plainly a material customer.
- The Seller offers reasonable endeavours, with the condition deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent. DD-002 cl 11.3 attaches **conditions** to that consent, and the Disclosure Letter (para 2) confirms that neither a final consent nor evidence that the conditions are satisfied has been provided.
- **Push back:** A condition precedent requiring:
  1. an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) consent under cl 11.2; and
  2. documentary evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, before Completion.
- Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient. Strengthen to an obligation to procure, or at minimum all reasonable endeavours with a Buyer walk right. Also consider a specific indemnity or price protection if Bluefen terminates or reprices for change of control.

### 10. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)
- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-of-control (cl 8.1) and discharge (cl 9.2) provisions. The Seller offers only a release "following Completion." Para 3 confirms there is no repayment and no discharge yet.
- A deferred release leaves security over the Company we are buying and creates a change-of-control default risk.
- **Push back:**
  - A current payout letter.
  - **Direct repayment from Completion funds** in the funds flow.
  - Executed or deliverable security releases (including PPSR discharges) at Completion.
- A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither currently exists.
- This also goes to debt-free/cash-free: the AUD 3.2m must be treated as Debt.

### 11. Employee bonuses (funds flow; DD-005)
- The draft funds flow states that the DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised. That is exactly the silent exclusion the playbook prohibits.
- These bonuses are triggered by Completion, so they become Company liabilities after Completion. Para 5 does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.
- **Push back:** Either a specific funds-flow line item paid at Completion through payroll (with withholding), or treatment as a Transaction Cost/Debt deducted from price. On-costs should be included as triggered. Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall or later-assessed on-costs.

### 12. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DD-004/DD-010)
- The Seller says the indemnity, limited to the SOW3 payment, is "adequate."
- The real exposure is that, under DD-004 cl 7.3, the SOW3 Project Materials **do not transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid**. There is no evidence of payment and no confirmatory assignment.
- The AUD 180,000 shown as open in DD-010 is **not independently verified either way**. We should not assume it is owed or that it has been paid.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or hold sufficient rights in the SOW3 materials, including third-party claims, re-development and remediation costs. It should not be confined to the fee.
  - Preserve the SOW3 cure mechanism, such as payment and a confirmatory assignment as a completion deliverable or CP.
  - Request bank or remittance evidence and Ironquay's confirmation of the account position.
  - The indemnity should sit outside the general cap and basket.

### 13. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
- The Seller calls this "preliminary... not expected to be material." On the facts disclosed (para 6), nothing establishes access, scope, harm, or whether a notification duty arises. The investigation is preliminary.
- We should neither accept the Seller's "not material" characterisation nor assert a confirmed breach or put a figure on it.
- **Push back:**
  - Pre-Completion covenants to preserve all logs and evidence.
  - Complete a proper investigation, including access logs for the download link.
  - Give us regular written updates and access to findings.
  - Take no notification or regulator decision without consulting us.
- Seek a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident, uncapped by the general regime or with a separate cap, and exclude it from deemed disclosure.

### 14. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000; DD-008/DD-011)
- The Seller calls them "ordinary-course operating costs." The disclosure itself (para 8) says it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. It also notes three related AUD 110k renewals to be read together, which may suggest the contract was split.
- **Position:** Assess them; do not concede either way. We should not automatically classify them as Debt or deduct them from price.
- **Action:** Request the renewal documents, commercial rationale, timing, termination rights and accrual treatment. Then decide whether they belong in working capital, Debt or a specific protection.

### 15. Tax and IP warranties
- The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." Under our playbook these terms remain **open**, and nothing has been resolved.
- **Push back:** State expressly that the tax and IP regimes are not agreed, and reserve our position. Keep them as separate categories, with a tax indemnity and its own claims period aligned to amendment periods. Do not assume unlimited liability.

### 16. Title evidence (DD-012)
- The Seller relies solely on the Company's own share register. Para 10 concedes this is the Seller's source and not Buyer verification.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence, including:
  - ASIC company extract and historical searches;
  - share certificates;
  - the issue and transfer history, with board minutes and constitution;
  - PPSR searches over the Seller and the shares;
  - confirmation that no options, convertibles or other rights to shares exist;
  - Seller authority documents (board resolution approving the sale and authorised signatories).

### 17. Other disclosure items to verify, not accept on characterisation
- **Office lease (DD-007):** The Seller says only a notification is required. We should confirm this by reviewing the lease ourselves and include the notice as a completion step.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The Seller says there is no consent requirement on a share sale. We should confirm independently that there is no change-of-control or deemed-assignment trigger.
- **Disclaimer (para 11):** Note this; it supports rejecting the general disclosures.

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m**; no fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k, excess only | **AUD 5k / AUD 50k, first-dollar tipping basket** |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months | **24 months** |
| 4 | Default limitation clause | Applies to all Claims | Delete; general regime for general warranties only |
| 5 | Title/Fundamental | General regime | **100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge** |
| 6 | Fraud | No carve-out | **Full carve-out; non-waivable** |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room and public records | **Specific fair disclosure only**; updated letter |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket exclusion | **Delete**; named persons and reasonable enquiry only |
| 9 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours, consent on delivery | **CP: effective consent plus evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are met** |
| 10 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | **Payout letter, repayment from funds flow, releases at Completion** |
| 11 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | **Line item or seller-funded, including on-costs, plus indemnity** |
| 12 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3 indemnity | **Broaden; preserve SOW3 cure; verify the AUD 180k** |
| 13 | DD-006 | "Not material" | **Preservation, investigation, updates covenants; specific indemnity**; no assumption either way |
| 14 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | **Assess**; no automatic Debt or deduction |
| 15 | Tax/IP | "Settled" | **Open; reserve; separate regimes** |
| 16 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent title and authority evidence** |

## Immediate next steps
1. Confirm with Amelia Frost that no principal-level agreement or fallback authority exists, and record it.
2. Send the Seller a short cover note stating the draft is not agreed and is open, and attaching our mark-up on the above.
3. Issue supplementary DD requests covering: Bluefen consent conditions, the Riverlark payout and releases, bonus on-cost calculations, Ironquay payment evidence, DD-006 logs and investigation status, the Sandbar documents, independent title searches, and a review of the lease and Mossvale clauses.
4. Require an updated Disclosure Letter, since the current one is dated 22 September 2026.
=== END ADVICE ===
